title: Part 10
html:
The Dhanvidhara thickets. Prabhasa. Dvaraka. The return journey: Baroda, the Narmada, farewell to Bharga, Dohad, Kukshi — the poor brahmana and the merchant's dream (pp. 183–202)

[p. 183]

2000Lions, tigers and all kinds of beasts live here;
thinking of it, I was very much afraid.

2001Understanding my mind from a hint,
the Lord smiled and said, "Why are you afraid for nothing?

2002If the Name of Hari removes the fear of Yama,
why are you afraid at the sight of these thickets?"

2003With our whole party we were sixteen people;
the son of Shachi entered the thickets.

2004The beauty of the jungle is most charming;
what can I say of its beauty — it would take long to tell.

2005How many wild flowers have bloomed, scenting the air,
how many hundreds of trees and creepers sway in the wind!

2006Sitting on the branches, birds of many kinds are singing;
hearing that song, the heart is overwhelmed.

2007Through the middle runs a single path, jungle on both sides,
and now and then bands of sannyasis appear.

2008I see the sun overhead,
and at once, for hunger, I look this way and that.

2009"To whose door shall I go now for alms?
There are no village people here — where shall I get alms?"

2010On both sides various trees are laden with fruit;
seeing the fruit, my eagerness grew.

[p. 184]

2011I cannot describe the wondrous fruit;
so many fruits have ripened and stand out in rows.

2012The fruit is shaped like a star-fruit;
never have I tasted fruit like it.

2013All around the fruit lies in heaps;
all the sannyasis are eating the fruit with both hands.

2014Without permission I cannot eat the fruit,
but seeing the fruit, greed seized me.

2015I take some fruit for the Lord,
and in the afternoon the Lord offers the fruit.

2016Having tasted two or four fruits,
Gora, the delight of hearts, tells us to eat.

2017I eat my fill of fruit, as much as I can,
and put as many more as I find into the bag.

2018Govinda Charana gobbles fruit after fruit,
while Ramananda tastes them slowly.

2019All saw the wondrous property of the fruit:
that wild fruit takes away both hunger and thirst.

2020On a tree like a four-sided cactus,
wondrous fruit — I eat it with great greed.

2021The more I eat, the more fruits I see;
I put more into the bag and eat till I am stuffed.

[p. 185]

2022In the dense jungle there is no smell of man;
now and then everyone raises the cry of "Hari".

2023Before evening had come it grew dark on the path;
the son of Shachi sat down beneath a tree.

2024Here and there the king has made halting-places;
we go down to one with the Lord.

2025A place fenced with forest logs, without house or door;
all the sannyasis sat down here.

2026Clapping his hands, the Lord began the Name,
and hearing the Name, the sannyasis grew excited.

2027Gathering wood, they lit a fire;
Bhargadeva chants the Name, clapping his hands.

2028In the middle of that jungle we feel no fear;
chanting the Name of Hari, we all pass the night.

2029Next morning, raising the cry of "Hari",
Gora set out, remembering Sri Hari.

2030The further we go, the denser the jungle;
seeing those thickets, the body trembles.

2031Going a long way, we find a small stream,
and there Shachi's darling bathes.

2032Having bathed, we hurry on ahead
and, after going some distance, all sit down.

[p. 186]

2033The Lord tells Ramananda to bring fruit,
and Ramananda brings fruit and puts it down there.

2034He gathers and brings fruits of every kind,
and Gora, the delight of hearts, worships and makes the offering.

2035Never have I seen such sweet fruit;
all together we fill our bellies with fruit.

2036Food for thousands of people lies on the road;
to whom shall I tell how great God's mercy is!

2037Finishing our tasks by midday, we go on,
and in the afternoon we all find another halting-place.

2038A place at the edge of the jungle, fenced with stakes;
there Gora, the delight of hearts, entered.

2039Bringing wood, the sannyasis lit a fire,
and the Lord, clapping his hands, began the song:

2040"Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Hare Krishna, Hare" —
this song the Lord sings at any hour.

2041As he sang I saw that he was beside himself;
the Lord was filled with thrills and his body trembled.

2042Gora Raya began to weep aloud,
and seeing his state Bharga cried out.

2043Next day, rising in the morning, we go on;
on the road a band of pilgrims comes back towards us.

[p. 187]

2044When the two bands met on the road,
all joyfully raised the cry of "Hari".

2045Thus in seven days the Dhanvidhara thickets
we all crossed, spreading joy.

2046Nearby is Amarapuri, named Gopitala;
we all go there, to the abode of joy.

2047Everyone calls this the holy place of Prabhasa;
seeing Prabhasa, I felt great delight.

2048Where the Yadus gave up their bodies,
there the Lord went and wept a great deal.

2049Drunk on mead, all the Yadu heroes
fought one another and gave up their bodies.

2050Without counting who was kin and who a stranger,
by Krishna's will the Yadu heroes died.

2051Charudeshna, Sura, Satyaki, Yuyudhana,
Samba, Gada and all the other wise ones

2052died there, fighting one another;
with a sorrowful face the Lord weeps at that place.

2053No one gains so much joy from weeping:
weeping, the Lord scatters bliss over the earth.

2054To take away the grief and sorrow of the world,
he preaches the Name of Hari at all times.

[p. 188]

2055The Name of Hari, love, devotion, the worship of Hari —
these the Lord teaches the people of the world unceasingly.

2056Day or night, he goes from door to door
and distributes the Name of Hari throughout the world:

2057"Who will take the Name of Hari? Come forward!
I give everyone this jewel without price.

2058All of you, take this priceless jewel with care,
and you will cross the ocean of worldly existence without effort.

2059If once you utter the Name of Hari with your lips,
your bonds will be cut and all will go to the eternal abode.

2060Very tight are the knots of the rope of maya;
who can cut them but with the sword of the Name of Hari?"

2061Saying this, the Lord goes from door to door
and spreads the rasa of love through the world.

2062The people of Amarapuri gathered together
and all were delighted to see the Lord.

2063Like a madman he runs this way and that,
roaming about intoxicated with ecstasy.

2064Sometimes he runs breathlessly, as if senseless,
the pupils of his eyes rolled upwards.

2065The mass of his matted hair has fallen loose over his back,
and tears fall ceaselessly onto his breast.

[p. 189]

2066Dressed like a madman, his garment slipping,
chalk flying all over his body, grey with dust.

2067"Where is the sacrificial pit?" says Gora Raya,
and the pandas, staying with him, show him Prabhasa.

2068We go to the southern part of Prabhasa
and there we see the pit.

2069Having dug this pit, the Lord of the Yadus performed a sacrifice,
and at that sacrifice the Yadus fought and died.

2070Where Satyabhama made a garden
and sometimes came there with Krishna,

2071where the virtuous lady lived in supreme joy —
seeing that place, the great-souled Gauranga

2072burst into tears, crying aloud;
crying out again and again, the Lord weeps without end.

2073Gradually ten pandas gathered
and one by one began showing all the places.

2074After three days of spiritual conversation here,
he then told us to go on to the city of Dvaraka.

2075At Prabhasa there are no more tirthas to see;
on the first of Ashvin we go to Dvaraka.

2076The Lord goes chanting Krishna's name;
along the seashore we go to Dvaraka.

[p. 190]

2077After four days we come to an inlet of the sea;
it has to be crossed on a rope.

2078Over the rope we cross to Dvaraka
and see a mountain called Raivataka.

2079Seeing the mountain, Gora sways with feeling,
and the Lord smiled quietly.

2080Who knows why, with a radiant face,
Mahaprabhu looked at me with a smile.

2081Looking at me he said, "When you reach Dvaraka,
bow down, all of you, and be fulfilled.

2082With great devotion smear the dust all over your bodies;
by the fruit of your merit you have seen the city of Dvaraka.

2083By the strength of good deeds in former lives
you have all seen the city of Dvaraka today."

2084Hearing this, all of us bowed down together,
and Gora's well of joy overflowed.

2085Saying "Hari bol, Hari bol",
the Lord gradually came down, swaying.

2086The ocean of feeling surged, overstepping all bounds;
who could hold the Lord back now?

2087Rolling over and over, he falls on the ground,
and gradually he entered the city.

[p. 191]

2088His hair stood on end and he began to tremble,
and tears seemed to burst from his eyes.

2089"Where are you, Lord of Dvaraka?" — saying this,
he flooded the land of Dvaravati with tears.

2090Everything in disarray, his matted hair came loose,
and Gora burst into very loud weeping.

2091What can I say of his state — it is beyond words;
again and again the Lord cries out, "Krishna!"

2092When he entered the house of the Lord of Dvaraka,
at once he grew twice as drunk with joy.

2093His body bristled like a kadamba,
rolling over and over he falls, grey with dust.

2094Drunk with feeling, the Lord gazes languidly
and lies rolling on the ground before the Lord of Dvaraka.

2095All around, devotion seems to overflow;
my Gora, the delight of hearts, weeps and sobs.

2096Sometimes, closing his eyes, he looks within,
as if he were seeing something in his heart.

2097Sometimes he stands gazing upwards,
tears streaming down from his eyes.

2098Seeing Krishna, his body was filled with thrills,
and he gazed at him fixedly.

[p. 192]

2099He circles the holy temple three times,
bowing humbly each time.

2100Gora, the delight of hearts, bows with all eight limbs,
and seeing this Bhargadeva falls prostrate.

2101Gradually word spread through Dvaraka,
and everyone whispered about the Lord.

2102Some say, "Come and see the sannyasi, brother;
no one has ever seen such a sannyasi.

2103What can I say of him — it is beyond words;
surely there is no other sannyasi like him on earth.

2104Never have I seen such a wondrous state;
I would give my life for the sannyasi's beauty and virtues!

2105Seeing him, devotion arises in the heart,
and tears come into the eyes of themselves.

2106I long to go away with the sannyasi;
if you see him, brother, your bonds are cut.

2107Seeing him, one loses all taste for worldly life;
seeing that form, a sinner becomes pure at once.

2108No one so merciful is to be seen;
in his mercy he gives the Name of Hari to all.

2109A head full of matted hair, an outer cloth for clothing;
seeing his form, one's desires are fulfilled.

[p. 193]

2110Seeing him, one feels he is an incarnation of God;
his heart is always full of the rasa of devotion.

2111The young sannyasi is always drunk with this ecstasy;
he has stirred up the people of Dvaraka.

2112He has no lust, no anger, no desire;
his faith in the Lord of Dvaraka is unshakeable.

2113He calls the sinners and gives them the Name of Hari;
seeing him, the heart overflows."

2114Gora Raya stayed a fortnight in Dvaraka
and went every day to the Lord of Dvaraka.

2115Every day he went and had darshan to his heart's content,
and made the city of Dvaraka drunk with the rasa of devotion.

2116All the people of Dvaraka who were devoted to God
come to see the Lord.

2117The Lord holds spiritual conversation with all,
and all, singing kirtana, dance full of love.

2118The city sways with the spirit of dharma;
everyone's heart seems to have become pure.

2119A gentle breeze always began to blow,
and everything around was fragrant with lotus.

2120All the people rejoice in the Lord's company;
women and men alike come running.

[p. 194]

2121On all sides auspicious signs appeared;
through the Name of Hari every quarter grew bright.

2122Pandas and householders all together
listen to the teaching on dharma with attentive ears.

2123He explains to anyone who does not understand;
speaking in many tongues, the Lord inspires him.

2124Sometimes my Lord speaks "khai mai",
speaks "jhi mai"1 and explains to everyone.

2125How he makes the people understand — he is all-powerful;
hearing his teaching, all were beside themselves.

2126Wise men and fools alike all came,
and seeing the Lord, all were thrilled.

2127One evening the Lord slowly
went to the temple of Krishna.

2128Many people follow behind the Lord,
but Shachi's son says nothing, good or bad.

2129At the temple door he made the eight-limbed obeisance,
and seeing this all the people rolled on the ground.

2130With folded hands the Lord sings many hymns,
and at once tears pour from his eyes.

2131The Lord's heart brims with the rasa of love:
wherever he looks he sees everything full of Krishna.

[p. 195]

2132Closing his eyes, he began to call, "Krishna!"
and his body thrilled with love.

2133One who has not seen that state with his own eyes —
how shall I, a great fool, make him understand?

2134Where there was no [water], a desert,
there Chaitanya Gosai made a river flow.

2135In the whole country no sinner remained;
by giving devotion, the Lord delivered the sinners.

2136One day the pandas, rejoicing,
held a great festival, making an offering.

2137Inviting guests and Vaishnavas,
they distribute thickened milk, yogurt, puris and the rest.

2138Gora, the jewel of virtues, going among the pandas,
distributes the prasada himself.

2139At night we all go together to the hut
and pass the night in supreme joy.

2140Thus, after a fortnight of spiritual conversation,
the next day the Lord leaves the city of Dvaraka.

2141The Lord said, "This time we shall go to Nilachala,
and in Nilachala we shall all live together in joy.

2142Come, let us all go together to Vidyanagara;
I will not go to Puri alone, leaving Rama Raya behind.

[p. 196]

2143Ramananda is a great lover of worship;
when I think of him my heart is soothed.

2144Ramananda Raya is the crest-jewel of practitioners;
sitting in solitude, Raya sings the glories of Krishna.

2145One whose tears flow at the name of Hari-Krishna
the Bhagavata calls an eternal Vaishnava.

2146If even a fool calls on the treasure that is Krishna with devotion,
I bow millions of times at his feet.

2147Ramananda, the devotee of Krishna, is worthy of worship;
Ramananda Raya is dearer to me than life.

2148I love Ramananda as my own life;
he is a supreme Vaishnava, a detached sannyasi.

2149Rama Raya is unattached to worldly things;
every day Raya gets to see Radha and Krishna.

2150Ramananda counts wealth as straw
and calls on Krishna with love day and night.

2151I have seen that, as he calls out "Krishna",
Raya, drunk with love, keeps trembling.

2152At Krishna's name he sheds tears of love
and falls unconscious on the ground.

2153My heart can bear separation from Raya no longer;
let us all go quickly to Raya."

[p. 197]

2154Saying this, the Lord set out,
and hundreds of people followed him.

2155Sending the village people back with sweet words,
my Gora Raya goes towards the inlet.

2156Bhargadeva with his party
comes to the bank of the inlet to cross.

2157One by one, all having crossed,
my sannyasi of Nadia comes into Gujarat.

2158On the last day of Ashvin, coming back to the city of Baroda,
my Lord chants the Name of Hari.

2159Govinda Charana and I, to beg alms,
presented ourselves at householders' doors.

2160Fruits, roots, flour, parched grain — whatever alms I receive,
I bring and offer with a pure heart.

2161Settling beneath a tree, the Lord made the offering,
and receiving the prasada, all were fulfilled.

2162Next day, setting out from Baroda,
the Lord began to go south.

2163After sixteen days we came to the bank of the Narmada,
and all of us bathed in the waters of the Narmada.

2164The Lord said, "Bhargadeva, where will you go?
Will you come with me to Nilachala?"

[p. 198]

2165Bharga, before the Lord, rubbing his hands,
said, "I shall go south.

2166In the city of Bom-bom2 the mahanta Aditya Raj
serves Ranchhodji with devotion.

2167Accept my obeisance, Lord;
mercifully place your foot on my head."

2168Saying this, Bhargadeva fell prostrate
and clasped both feet tightly with both hands.

2169Bharga said, "You are Krishna, you are my Hari;
give me this alms: that I may die remembering your feet.

2170To see your own lilas and play yourself,
you went to Dvaraka, deceiving people.

2171Be that as it may, put your foot on my head;
you will not be able to deceive me again — I will not be deceived."

2172The Lord said, "Bharga, why do you say such things?
Why do you speak such words to me?

2173I wander the roads as a renunciant,
without food, without clothing, utterly poor and lowly.

2174For alms I go from door to door;
never speak such words to me again.

2175Always say 'Krishna, Krishna' with faith;
faith in Krishna will bring you to Krishna.

[p. 199]

2176Hari is a mass of consciousness and bliss, the highest of the high;
meditate on his lotus feet and you will cross the ocean of existence.

2177With love and devotion meditate on Hari's feet,
and he will surely show himself to you.

2178Hari is very kind to his devotees;
think of him — he is the refuge of the helpless."

2179Saying this, the Lord touched Bhargadeva,
and at once Bharga's body was purified.

2180Standing on the bank, Bhargadeva gazes at him
and, fulfilled, at last took his leave.

2181All the other sannyasis who were with Bharga
came and stood before the Lord.

2182One by one they bowed at the Lord's feet,
and the Lord sent them all off with sweet words.

2183Bhargadeva went away to the south,
and the Lord sets out lovingly for Nilachala.

2184I, Ramananda and Govinda Charana
spent that day on the bank of the Narmada.

2185Next day we go along the bank of the Narmada
and all arrive at the town of Dohad.

2186I brought some flour that I had begged,
and Lord Gaura-Hari made rotis and offered them.

[p. 200]

2187We pass the night in the town of Dohad;
beneath a tree Gora-chand raises the cry of "Hari".

2188Rising in the morning, we go to the town of Kukshi,
and here we see many Vaishnavas.

2189Wherever we go we see tulasi groves;
every villager, I see, is devoted to Krishna.

2190In the evening all the people raise the cry of "Hari";
seeing this, my Lord thrills with joy.

2191In this place lives a poor brahmana,
and in his house there is Lakshmi-Janardana.

2192The brahmana worships Lakshmi-Janardana with devotion;
hearing of this, the Lord goes to his house.

2193The brahmana, seeing the Lord, offers him hospitality,
welcoming him warmly, regarding him as a guest.

2194The brahmana says, "I am a poor brahmana;
why have you set foot in my house?

2195How shall I serve a sannyasi?
I fear my dharma will be ruined in my house."

2196The Lord said, "Have no anxiety, thakura:
he whose creation it is will give food in plenty.

2197Who worries for whom — that is the error of Kali;
hear the essence: it is Krishna who always cares.

[p. 201]

2198The householder says, 'I feed everyone';
but who thinks how the homeless man living under a tree is fed?

2199Who gives food to the tiny insects in the forest?
Why then, brahmana, do you worry for nothing?"

2200Just then a vaishya3 came to the brahmana's door
bringing milk, sugar and flour to fill his store.

2201The vaishya said, "Listen, listen, brahmana thakura:
the Lord has shown me his mercy.

2202I saw your Janardana in a dream:
he asks me for sweet rice.

2203In the form of a man Narayana is your guest;
Narayana showed me this in a dream.

2204Last night, before dawn, I saw it in a dream,
and I have brought milk and sugar for his sake.

2205Cook sweet rice and offer it to Narayana, brahmana."
Hearing this, the brahmana began to weep.

2206The brahmana said, "Where have the milk and sugar come from?"
The Lord said, "Narayana himself has provided them."

2207[Here came] milk and sugar [the line is corrupt in the edition].
The brahmana said, "I am a poor man — this is a marvel!"

2208The Lord said, "Narayana…" [the line breaks off].
The brahmana said, "I was worrying about you."

2209The Lord said, "Narayana has given and provided."4

[p. 202]

2210The vaishya, gazing at the Lord's face,
sees something, losing consciousness again and again.

2211The brahmana said, "Vaishya, what are you seeing, brother?"
The vaishya said, "I am bewildered, that is why I look.

2212Listen, best of brahmanas, what shall I tell you:
in my dream I saw him in human form."

2213Hearing this, the Lord said to the vaishya,
"Why do you keep making a fuss for nothing?

2214Whom did you see in an empty dream?
Why then do you make a fuss without reason?

2215Brother vaishya, you are a holy man and very fortunate;
that is why the Lord Bhagavan appeared to you in a dream.

2216I am an ordinary sannyasi, come
to a brahmana's house for the sake of food."

2217The brahmana said, "What need is there for such talk?
Narayana takes care of the service of guests."

2218Then the brahmana, weeping, begged the Lord,
"Cook the sweet rice yourself and make the offering."

2219With a slight smile the Lord cooked the sweet rice,
and the brahmana, staying near, waited upon him.

2220All received the prasada with joy;
the Lord distributed the prasada with his own hands.

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. "Khai mai", "jhi mai": Govinda imitates the sound of languages unknown to him (Gujarati, Kathiawari).
  2. "Bom-bom nagar" is apparently Bombay (Mumbai), as D. C. Sen suggests.
  3. A vaishya is a member of the merchant class.
  4. Lines 2207–2209 are badly damaged in the edition (some words are missing); the translation gives the surviving sense.
